criteria.text: The response identifies that the Software License Agreement renews automatically for successive 36-month Renewal Terms unless non-renewal notice is given within a 15-day Non-Renewal Window ending 120 days before term end, which departs from the term sheet's 12-month renewals terminable on 60 days' notice. It locates this in the Software License Agreement (Section 2.2 and/or the Section 1 definitions), explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the exclusivity covenant in Software License Agreement Section 3.5 is broader than the term sheet's LIMS-only, US Licensed Sites, term-only exclusivity. The response must show that the covenant covers diagnostic imaging and practice-management software, applies at any facility worldwide (including Affiliates' facilities), and continues for 24 months after the term. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that, because Amendment No. 1 restates Section 11 so that Section 11.1 is now the Licensee's indemnity, the liability-cap carve-out for 'amounts payable under Section 11.1' now leaves the client's (Licensee's) indemnity uncapped. It locates this in Software License Agreement Section 13.2 or Amendment No. 1 Section 2, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the side letter's broader definition of 'Connected Instrument', which includes devices transmitting data to the Software such as point-of-care devices at Partner Clinics, governs the Software License Agreement's instrument overage fee. The response must conclude that this exposes the client to $1,800-per-year overage fees on partner-clinic devices above the 120-instrument count. It locates this in Side Letter Section 2 or Software License Agreement Section 4.4/18.3, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Software License Agreement's Initial Term is 36 months from the April 1, 2026 Effective Date (ending March 31, 2029).
The response states that under the Software License Agreement's order-of-precedence clause, amendments and the Side Letter prevail over the Software License Agreement in the event of a conflict.
The response is formatted as a memo addressed to the supervising partner. For each issue it sets out the location (document and section), why the issue matters for Pupeska, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that the Licensee indemnity added by Amendment No. 1 remains subject to the Section 13.1 liability cap under the documents as they currently stand.
The response claims that the term sheet's renewal or exclusivity terms currently bind the parties and override the broader terms of the signed Software License Agreement.
